day_shape: 76 items: regime channels claim missile/drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan with Pentagon confirming one US soldier killed at Erbil and ~100 wounded since hostilities resumed, France summons Iran's chargé over detained diplomats, Jerusalem Post reports Tehran-initiated 10-day ceasefire proposal, IDF eliminates two Hamas October 7 commanders.

threads.label: Gulf base attacks and US casualties
threads.summary: Regime channels claimed drone and missile strikes on US facilities at Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, in Kuwait, and at Al-Rukban in Jordan, with IRIB citing sirens in Bahrain and Kuwait and posting satellite images of Muwaffaq al-Salti. Pentagon Spokesperson Sean Parnell said nearly 100 US service members have been wounded since hostilities resumed, and named Sergeant Michael Swimton, 30, as killed at Erbil.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and Gulf shipping
threads.summary: IRIB claimed the number of ships awaiting Iran's permission to transit the Strait of Hormuz has increased and reported three vessels on the 'American route' had accidents, alongside Al-Alam reports two Saudi tankers diverted from Bab al-Mandeb to Suez. Khamenei's office posted a poster warning foreigners in the Gulf 'have no place except at its bottom', while Pakistan's PM voiced concern and Reuters cited Saudi May crude exports at historic lows.

threads.label: US-Iran ceasefire and diplomatic track
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Tehran initiated the 10-day US-Iran ceasefire proposal now under discussion, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said a six-person SNSC subcommittee handled decisions on the defunct MoU. Defa Press cited former NCTC head Joseph Kent urging Washington to accept 'strategic coexistence' with Iran, while Iranian conservative media attacked Araghchi's interview.

threads.label: France-Iran diplomatic rupture
threads.summary: The French foreign ministry summoned Iran's chargé d'affaires two days after saying French embassy staff had been detained and physically intimidated by Iranian security services in Tehran. Iran International reported Paris is weighing a reduction of its Tehran embassy staffing following the incident.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and Hamas leadership
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing of Adham Ibrahim Sha'aban Nasman, Hamas's Gaza City Brigade operations chief who directed the October 7 infiltration and held hostages, plus cell commander Osama Kamal Shehadeh Abu Teim involved in the Cooper and Dancyg abductions. New Hamas political bureau head Khalil al-Hayya issued his first message, and Jerusalem Post reported IDF construction of a 23km sand barrier inside Gaza.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon 'Safe Zone' friction
threads.summary: The Lebanese Armed Forces said IDF troops opened fire near Lebanese army forces deploying in Zawtar al-Gharbiya during implementation of the Safe Zone pilot programme, from which Israel is withdrawing. Trump hosted Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the White House — the first such visit in over 17 years.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures: executions, economy, power
threads.summary: Iran International reported a Shiraz Revolutionary Court sentenced two men to death for aiding wounded January protesters, authorities secretly buried teenage protester Erfan Esfandiyari, and economists warned war is tipping malaise into crisis with a possible petrol price rise under discussion. IRIB reported industrialists at an Industry Day event citing power cuts as their main problem, with President Pezeshkian saying he ordered cuts to government but not industrial electricity.
